text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak, Crown Prince Abdullah of Saudi Arabia and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat held a joint session of talks in Cairo on Wednesday and Arafat explained the situation in the occupied territories.
- Mubarak met European Union special envoy Miguel Angel Moratinos. Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said Moratinos explained the European position on the Middle East peace process.
- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright will meet Egyptian presidential adviser Osama el-Baz in Washington tomorrow to discuss Egyptian efforts to save the peace process.
- Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid said there was good demand for public-sector companies offered for sale in May, with share offers covered between six and 73 times over.
- Agriculture Minister Youssef Wali said a World Bank mission was now visiting Egypt to discuss Egypt's needs for financing the project to develop the New Valley.

- The meeting between Mubarak, Arafat and Prince Abdullah discussed the latest developments in the peace process, efforts to move it forward, the situation in the Arab world and how to reactivate Arab solidarity.

- Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid said a new strategy has been prepared to increase exports of pharmaceuticals to 250 million pounds ($75 million) and to concentrate on opening new markets in Eastern Europe and Arab countries.
- Electricity Minister Maher Abaza asked investors to increase their investements in new and renewable power projects and in manufacturing electrical equipment locally.
- The Ministry of Reconstruction and Cairo province have started to implement President Mubarak's instructions to finish off the Cairo ring road quickly.

- Arab League Secretary-General Esmat Abdel-Meguid indicated that there would be a joint Arab and African move to solve the problem of Lockerbie in the light of new proposals which he refused to disclose.
